- Model consistently overestimates early in the forecast horizon, especially in the first 5–10 days, then underestimates later days.
- Forecasts tend to overshoot after sharp price spikes (e.g., 65+ → 70+), then correct downward, suggesting model fails to capture momentum decay.
- Mean reversion is underemphasized — model holds high forecasts longer than actual price tends to revert toward recent 30-day average.
- Model exhibits lag in responding to recent low prices — when history includes recent dips, forecasts still show upward bias.
- Forecasts often ignore the influence of the most recent 5–7 days in the history window, leading to persistent overestimation.
- Model tends to overreact to short-term volatility, especially when price spikes occur in the last 7–10 days of history.
- Forecasts are too optimistic in the first 10 days, then too pessimistic in the last 10 days — suggesting asymmetric bias toward early optimism.
- Model fails to adjust for seasonal or calendar-driven patterns (e.g., end-of-month or quarter-end price behavior) — often underestimates price spikes near these dates.
